q: Which Scope 3 categories are mandatory to report, and can I leave some out?
title: Which Scope 3 categories are mandatory?
short: No single category is mandatory for everyone. The GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard requires you to account for all relevant categories and to disclose and justify any you exclude. What becomes mandatory depends on who asks: SBTi target coverage, IFRS S2, CSRD or a buyer's questionnaire each set their own rule.

ul: Scope 3 is optional under the Corporate Standard. It becomes required only if you claim to follow the Scope 3 Standard.
If you do, you must account for Scope 3 emissions across the 15 categories, report each relevant category separately, and disclose and justify any exclusion.

Relevance is judged by size, influence, risk, stakeholder interest, outsourcing and sector guidance (Table 6.1). A category can be left out only if it does not apply or is not relevant on these tests.
SBTi near-term criteria: if Scope 3 is 40% or more of total Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, the Scope 3 target must cover at least 67% of Scope 3 emissions.
IFRS S2: disclose Scope 3 emissions and which of the 15 categories are included, using the GHG Protocol; a first-year relief lets entities defer Scope 3.
CSRD (ESRS E1): disclose significant Scope 3 categories, with the scope now limited by the 2026 simplification of who must report.
BRSR: Scope 3 sits among the leadership indicators, which are voluntary for listed companies.
Buyers: an EU customer may ask only for your Scope 1 and 2 and the product footprint of what you sell them.

ol: Screen every category with a rough estimate, even spend-based.
Mark categories that do not apply, for example franchises for a factory with none.
For small categories, record the estimate and the reason, such as below 1% of the total in your screening.
Write the exclusion and reason in the report so a reader or verifier can test it.
Rescreen when the business changes, for example a new product line or outsourced logistics.

sections.h: Categories that usually matter for Indian manufacturers
p: Category 1 purchased goods, Category 3 fuel and energy related activities, Category 4 upstream transport, Category 5 waste and, for exporters on delivered terms, outbound freight. For makers of motors, pumps or vehicles, Category 11 use of sold products can be the largest of all.

example.title: Worked example: does the SBTi 67% rule apply?
lines: Scope 1: 800 t CO2e; Scope 2: 1,200 t CO2e; Scope 3 screening: 6,000 t CO2e
Target must cover at least 67% of 6,000 = 4,020 t CO2e of Scope 3

senseible: Senseible separates Scope 3 lines from your invoices into a supplier evidence trail, so you can see which categories have documented data. It does not screen categories you hold no documents for or decide which exclusions a framework will accept.
